page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv7 general-purpose family, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is configured with 16 dedicated 64-bit ARM (arm64) vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features no graphics accelerators, directing all processing capacity to general-purpose and compute-focused ARM tasks.

A primary hardware component of this configuration is the bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral storage alongside support for external Azure Premium Storage volumes. Networking setups rely on private virtual interfaces, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Due to its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and onboard NVMe disk, the D16plds_v7 offers cost efficiency for workloads constrained more by compute capability and fast scratch storage than large volatile memory spaces. It is well-fitted for CI/CD build runners, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and distributed application components that benefit from ARM energy efficiency and high-speed temporary disk caching.
